# Incident Report — 2024-11-26 Traffic Analysis Exercise

## Victim host
| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 | 10.11.26.183 |
| MAC | d0:57:7b:ce:fc:8b |
| Windows hostname | DESKTOP-B8TQK49 (NetBIOS workgroup/domain NEMOTODES; AD domain nemotoads.health, DC NEMOTODE-DC/NEMOTODES-DC at 10.11.26.3) |
| Logged-in user | oboomwald (from Kerberos AS-REQ CNameString between 10.11.26.183 and the DC 10.11.26.3) |

## Malware family
**NetSupport RAT** — the legitimate NetSupport Manager remote-control client, trojanized/repurposed for covert C2. **Signature-confirmed**, on two independent lines of evidence:

1. Suricata alerts directly name it: `ETPRO TROJAN NetSupport RAT CnC Activity` (65 hits), `ETPRO TROJAN Malicious NetSupport Rat CnC Checkin` (2 hits), `ET INFO NetSupport Remote Admin Checkin`/`Response`, and `ET POLICY NetSupport GeoLocation Lookup Request`, all against 10.11.26.183.
2. Independently, I pulled the raw bytes of the HTTP POST bodies to `194.180.191.64/fakeurl.htm` and they show NetSupport Manager's exact client check-in grammar: `CMD=POLL\nINFO=1\nACK=1\n` and `CMD=ENCD\nES=1\nDATA=<binary>`. This is the documented NetSupport protocol, not a guess from the alert name.

## Infection chain (from DNS/TLS SNI/HTTP evidence, in order)
1. **08:50:11 UTC** — TLS connection to `classicgrand.com` (213.246.109.5), ~3.4 MB transferred. Acts as a gate/redirector.
2. **08:50:14 UTC** — DNS lookup and TLS connection to `modandcrackedapk.com` (193.42.38.139), flagged by Suricata as `ET CURRENT_EVENTS ZPHP Domain in DNS Lookup` and `...in TLS SNI`. ~11 MB transferred over this encrypted session — consistent with the NetSupport client package being downloaded here. The domain name (a fake "mod and cracked APK" download site) indicates the lure was pirated/cracked software.
3. **08:50:14 UTC** — parallel TLS session to `confirmsubscription.com` (52.8.34.0) and `css/js.createsend1.com` — a browser push-notification subscription scam typically bundled with these cracked-download sites. This is adware/PUP noise from the same site visit, not part of the RAT's C2, so it's listed separately below.
4. **08:50:45 UTC** — the newly installed NetSupport client performs a legitimate startup geolocation lookup: `GET /location/loca.asp HTTP/1.1` to `geo.netsupportsoftware.com` (104.26.1.231) — genuine NetSupport vendor infrastructure, not attacker-controlled, but it's the tell that the dropped binary is the real NetSupport Manager client.
5. **08:50:45 UTC onward** — the client begins beaconing to the attacker's C2 at `194.180.191.64` over plaintext HTTP on port 443 (`POST /fakeurl.htm`), roughly every 60 seconds, continuing through the end of the capture (~09:43 UTC), i.e. over 50 minutes of active C2.

## Indicators of Compromise

| Type | Value | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| C2 endpoint | 194.180.191.64:443 (HTTP, not TLS despite the port) | Repeated `POST /fakeurl.htm` with body `CMD=POLL\nINFO=1\nACK=1\n` and `CMD=ENCD\nES=1\nDATA=...`; matches ETPRO TROJAN NetSupport RAT CnC alerts |
| URL | http://194.180.191.64/fakeurl.htm | Captured HTTP request lines, ~65+ POSTs over the session |
| Domain | modandcrackedapk.com → 193.42.38.139 | DNS query + TLS Client Hello SNI at 08:50:14/08:50:40; `ET CURRENT_EVENTS ZPHP Domain` alerts; ~11 MB payload transfer immediately preceding infection |
| Domain | classicgrand.com → 213.246.109.5 | DNS query + TLS SNI at 08:50:11; ~3.4 MB transfer; precedes and redirects into modandcrackedapk.com |
| Domain (benign vendor infra, diagnostic of the RAT) | geo.netsupportsoftware.com → 104.26.1.231 | `GET /location/loca.asp`; `ET POLICY NetSupport GeoLocation Lookup Request` alert |

**File names / SHA256 hashes:** none captured. The payload delivered from modandcrackedapk.com (193.42.38.139) was downloaded entirely over TLS 1.2/1.3 with no plaintext HTTP file transfer observed anywhere in the capture, so no dropped file name or hash could be extracted from traffic. All HTTP-exported objects in the capture are small legitimate Microsoft/Adobe housekeeping files (connecttest.txt, ProcessMAU.txt, OCSP/CRL blobs, disallowedcertstl.cab, authrootstl.cab) plus the tiny NetSupport check-in bodies — nothing resembling an executable.

## Benign/adware context (not the RAT, do not treat as C2)
- confirmsubscription.com (52.8.34.0), css.createsend1.com / js.createsend1.com (18.160.156.x) — browser push-notification subscription scam popup, common on cracked-software gate pages.
- www.msftconnecttest.com, licensing.mp.microsoft.com, client.wns.windows.com, windows.msn.com, officeclient.microsoft.com, www.bing.com, login.live.com, nav/data-edge.smartscreen.microsoft.com, r10.o.lencr.org, ctldl.windowsupdate.com, acroipm2.adobe.com/armmf.adobe.com, fonts.googleapis.com/gstatic.com, code.jquery.com, resources.office.net, events.data.microsoft.com — standard Windows/Office/Adobe/browser telemetry, update, and certificate-revocation traffic.
- SMB/NBNS/LDAP/Kerberos/DCE-RPC traffic between 10.11.26.183 and the DC (10.11.26.3), including the `[MS-EFSR] EfsRpcOpenFileRaw` and SMBv1 alerts — reviewed directly in the capture; no lateral-movement or coercion attempt pattern was found in that traffic (no matching efsr-tagged frames returned on direct filter), consistent with normal domain-joined authentication chatter rather than an active attack, though it remains unusual to see SMBv1/legacy NTLMSSP alerts on an enterprise LAN and is worth a hardening review independent of this infection.

## Incident summary
The Windows workstation DESKTOP-B8TQK49 (10.11.26.183, MAC d0:57:7b:ce:fc:8b), logged in as domain user oboomwald, was infected with NetSupport RAT after browsing to a fake cracked-software/mod-APK site (classicgrand.com redirecting to modandcrackedapk.com) around 08:50 UTC on 2024-11-26. The site delivered an ~11 MB payload over TLS that installed the NetSupport Manager client, which immediately began covert HTTP-based C2 beaconing to attacker infrastructure at 194.180.191.64 (POST /fakeurl.htm) roughly every 60 seconds for the remainder of the capture, giving the attacker remote-access capability over the host.
